summary: Recipes: the order the commands go in for each job an agent is sent to a course workspace to do. internal/cli/recipes.go is hand-authored and holds all six (move-to-new-term, accessibility-remediation, design-review, ai-use-map, build-from-materials, insert-image) as recipe{Name,Title,Summary,Steps}, each step a recipeStep{Say,Command,Line}: Say is the reason, Line is a runnable example, and Command is the command path the tests resolve against the live tree. `recipes` lists them and each recipe is its own subcommand, because whichIndex entries have to be real commands (TestWhichIndex_ExistsAndIsWellFormed runs root.Find over every entry), so a single `recipes <name>` command taking an argument could not be indexed. The parent's Args func turns an unknown name into an exit-2 usage error naming the real ones. internal/cli/root.go gains the AddCommand. internal/cli/which.go gains nine curated entries: check, upload, download, and one per recipe. internal/cli/sandbox_surface_test.go gains TestSandboxWhichOffersRecipesForItsJobs. SKILL.md gains a Canvas Builder mode section (what refuses and why, the course scope table, --job, approvals, the mode's own commands), the six recipes under Recipes, and exit codes 6, 8 and 9 in the table; README.md gains the recipes; CHANGELOG.md gains the Unreleased entry for the whole of Canvas Builder mode.
reason:
An agent can find any single command from `which` or `--help`. What it cannot find there is the order: that a course's own dates move before its assignment dates, that a page body is read before it is written back because the write replaces all of it, that an upload hands back the address a page must embed rather than a path on disk, and that nothing is finished until the checks run again. Every one of those is a mistake that looks like success until the instructor opens the course, so the order is the part worth writing down.

The entries in whichIndex matter as much as the recipes. Canvas Builder hides the six curated capabilities, all of which are built on student records, so visibleWhichIndex drops them and `which` is left answering out of the command tree alone — which offers 'courses create-file' for 'upload a file' and 'courses effective-due-dates' for 'shift due dates'. Both are the wrong answer inside Canvas Builder: the first is one of three steps, and the second reads dates rather than moving them. The nine new entries are what makes `which` useful in the mode the CLI now spends most of its life in.

The recipes are tested against the live command tree rather than reviewed, because a recipe is instructions an agent follows without checking them first. A flag that was renamed, or a command path that never existed, would be followed verbatim.
known_limitations:
The recipes name flags and command paths, and the tests check both against the tree, but nothing checks that a step's example would succeed against Canvas. A step could resolve, carry only real flags, and still send a request Canvas rejects; only the course-level tests and the checks catch that.

The [Check: ...] placeholders are a convention, not a mechanism. TestRecipePlaceholdersAreClosed only checks that each one is closed; an agent that pastes a line verbatim sends the literal text to Canvas. The alternative — refusing a value that looks like a placeholder — was not built, because the placeholder text is readable enough that the gateway's own validation and the checks report it, and a CLI-side rule would also catch an instructor who genuinely wrote square brackets in a page title.

recipeStep.Command is json:"-", so the JSON an agent reads carries only say and line. The command path exists for the tests. That means an agent cannot filter steps by command without parsing the line, which no caller needs today.

The which wording is tuned, not ranked: whichScoreEntry gives a description token +2 and the curated index a +1 boost, so an entry wins a query by containing its words. 'shift' and 'due' are in move-to-new-term's description for exactly that reason, and 'upload a file' is in upload's. A future rewording could lose a query without breaking anything else, which is why the six queries in TestWhichResolves and the four in TestSandboxWhichOffersRecipesForItsJobs assert the top match rather than mere presence.

The recipes name 'materials/' as the folder a file comes from. That is the Canvas Builder workspace layout (SPEC 4.3), not something this CLI enforces; outside Canvas Builder any path works, and inside it the upload refusal is what holds files to the workspace folder. A recipe's command lines are text, not code: nothing checks that a flag a step names still shortens or keeps a field the way the step says it does. The `--select url,title,body` on the two page reads is the example — if compactListFields later stops stripping body, the flag becomes redundant and the Say becomes wrong, and only a reader would notice.
validated_outcome:
go build ./... and go vet ./... clean. go test ./... passing across all nine packages on darwin/arm64 with Go 1.27.1 (internal/cli 0.968s). make build and make build-sandbox both produce a binary. gofmt -l is clean on every file in this patch; it still reports helpers.go and sync.go, which is the generator's own formatting and predates this patch.

golangci-lint run --max-issues-per-linter=0 --max-same-issues=0 ./internal/cli/ reports 549 issues, all of them the generator's pre-existing findings in generated files; nothing in recipes.go, recipes_test.go, which_search_test.go or the lines added to which.go, root.go and sandbox_surface_test.go. The first run reported 555: six errcheck findings on the new renderers in recipes.go, fixed by taking the _, _ = fmt.Fprintf form the other hand-authored renderers use (sandbox_surface.go's renderSandboxReport), with the argument-free call changed to fmt.Fprint so staticcheck has nothing to say about it either.

internal/cli/recipes_test.go holds seven tests, all against the live tree or through runCLI. TestRecipeStepsResolve: every recipe has a title, a summary and at least two steps; every step says something; a step with no command has no line; and for every step with a command, root.Find(strings.Fields(Command)) resolves with nothing left over, the line starts with 'canvas-pp-cli <Command>', and each --flag in the line is a flag of that command or a root persistent flag. TestRecipesEndWithChecksAndLabelWrites: the last step is 'check' and its line runs 'check all'; every write step carries '--job '. stepWrites reads the pp:method annotation, with nonGeneratedWrites covering upload, which is hand-authored and carries no method. TestRecipesReadBeforeTheyWrite: the first step with a command is not a write. TestRecipePlaceholdersAreClosed: every '[Check:' has a ']' after it. TestRecipesListsEveryRecipe, TestRecipeShowsSteps and TestRecipeUnknownNameIsUsage cover the command surface: the list envelope, one recipe's steps, and exit 2 with the real names on a wrong one. which_search_test.go's TestWhichResolves gains six rows for the new entries, and every existing row still passes. sandbox_surface_test.go gains TestSandboxWhichOffersRecipesForItsJobs, which asserts the top match for four job phrases inside Canvas Builder, where the curated student-data entries are gone. CodeRabbit (--agent --uncommitted --include-untracked) raised five findings on the recipes, all judged valid. One was a missing command: build-from-materials created a module and never put the page in it, so a `modules create-2` step was added. The other four were fixed in the recipe text: the two invented 2027 timestamps became [Check: ...] placeholders that keep the UTC format visible; the assignments read now asks for all_dates and the list-building step carries each override's own id, so a section's overridden due date moves with the rest; every page body now goes in through --stdin as {"wiki_page": {"body": ...}} rather than a double-quoted shell argument, because a page body is markup full of quotation marks; and each recipe's final step says what to do when `check all` exits 10 for a workspace with no closure days entered — run the other three checks by name and tell the instructor the date check is waiting. The exit-10 behaviour itself is a Canvas Builder question, not a CLI one, and is filed separately. A second CodeRabbit round raised three more, all valid and all fixed. The real one was that `--agent` means `--json --compact`, and compactListFields strips body from list rows, so both `pages index --include body --agent` reads were returning pages with no text: they now carry `--select url,title,body`, which printOutputWithFlags lets win over --compact, and each step says why the flag is there. The other two were documentation: SKILL.md now carries the no-closure-days fallback and the rule that a bulk-update list naming more than 500 assignments goes out as several lists under one job label. A third round left one finding, on the wording of that 500-assignment rule: written passively it read as a promise that the CLI splits a longer list, which it does not — the gateway refuses an over-long one with its generic "Canvas Builder doesn't let agents use this part of Canvas", which never mentions the length (that message is JR-57). Both the recipe step and SKILL.md now say the agent writes the lists itself and that the refusal will not tell it why. Final state: go vet, go test ./... (nine packages), make build and make build-sandbox all clean; gofmt reports only the pre-existing helpers.go and sync.go; golangci-lint on ./internal/cli/ holds at the 549 pre-existing generator findings.
